title: Intake day
scenario:
Your studio is filling the reference library for Bright Orchard, a juice brand. Six assets arrive on intake day. You check each record before anything goes into a set.

The intake sheet is made up for this case. It is our own format. This course gives no legal advice, so unclear cases go to the producer or a lawyer.
exhibit:
Intake sheet (made up)
  A-01  Bottle packshot. Client sent it by email on 3 March. Owner: client.
        Written OK for campaign use and AI reference use: yes, email on file.
        Valid until 2027-12-31.
  A-02  Stock photo of an orchard at dawn. Owner: stock site.
        Licence: web and social, 12 months, ends in 6 months.
        Use as an AI reference: not stated.
  A-03  Orange-slice drawing. A freelancer emailed the file. No contract on file.
  A-04  Photo of freelancer Lea holding a bottle. Permission: not recorded.
  A-05  Image made by the studio with Nano Banana 2.1, prompt log #88.
        Inputs: A-01 only. Use: campaign, as in the client brief.
        Owner and end date: as for A-01, per the client contract on file.
  A-06  Image found online. Note: "looks free".

File note
  A-01 arrived with Content Credentials. A designer resized it for a banner.
  The exported banner has none.

questions.prompt: Which assets can go into reference sets today?

options.text: A-01 and A-05: their records show the source, the use and the proof or the inputs.
options.explanation: Right. Their records are complete for this use. The others have an empty field, so they stay out until it is filled.

options.text: A-01, A-02 and A-05: the stock licence covers web use, so it must cover reference use too.
options.explanation: The record says use as an AI reference is not stated. A guess is not a record. Ask the producer or a lawyer.

options.text: A-01, A-03 and A-05: the freelancer emailed the drawing, which is a kind of agreement.
options.explanation: An email with a file does not record any terms. This course cannot judge it, so the producer or a lawyer must.

options.text: All six, and fill in any missing proof later if somebody asks about it.
options.explanation: Both Google and Runway put the duty to hold the rights on you. An empty field means the asset stays out.

questions.prompt: A-01's written OK ends on 2027-12-31. A copy sits in the Claude Files API. What is the best plan?

options.text: Set expires_in_seconds to the end date when uploading, so Claude removes the file on that date.
options.explanation: Anthropic's setting allows 3,600 seconds to 7,776,000 seconds (90 days). The end date is far above the maximum.

options.text: Do nothing. Files expire after a while by themselves, so the copy will be gone by then.
options.explanation: The Claude docs say files persist until you delete them or they reach an expires_at that you set.

options.text: Upload with a 90-day expiry and treat the expiry as proof that the content is deleted.
options.explanation: The Claude docs say expiration is a lifecycle feature, not a guaranteed-deletion control. Use DELETE to remove a file.

options.text: Record the end date in the catalogue, add a step to delete the copy by then, and mark A-01 retired.
options.explanation: Right. The expiry maximum is 90 days, so a date in the catalogue and a delete step do the job. DELETE removes the file.

questions.prompt: The banner made from A-01 has no Content Credentials. Where is the origin of A-01 recorded?

options.text: In the banner file. Credentials always survive editing, so the banner still carries them.
options.explanation: The OpenAI docs say editing, converting or sharing a file can remove its metadata. Here it did.

options.text: Nowhere is needed, because a SynthID watermark in the banner will show where it came from.
options.explanation: Google's docs say its generated images carry SynthID. A client's packshot photo was not generated by Google's models.

options.text: In the catalogue record, and in the untouched original that is kept safe in the archive.
options.explanation: Right. This is our habit: the source is written where an edit cannot remove it, and the original is kept as it arrived.

options.text: OpenAI's provenance check will prove the origin of the banner whenever somebody asks for it.
options.explanation: The OpenAI docs say the check looks only for OpenAI's own signals. It is not a general proof of origin.

questions.prompt: What goes into the record for A-05, the studio's AI-made image?

options.text: Only "AI-made", because the SynthID watermark already records everything else about it.
options.explanation: In our reading, a watermark marks the image. It does not record your prompt or the references you used.

options.text: The model and the date, the prompt log number, and every reference that was used, here A-01.
options.explanation: Right. This is our rule. The inputs of AI work can matter, so they are written down with it.

options.text: Nothing, because an AI-made image has no source and so there is nothing to write down.
options.explanation: It has a source: the model, the date, the prompt and the inputs. Those are what the record holds.

options.text: Only the designer's name, because the person who typed the prompt is the source of the image.
options.explanation: A name alone does not say which model, which prompt or which references were used.
